newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks mixed amid foreign fund interest.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks mixed amid foreign fund interest.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in sessions driven by foreign funds, traders said Wednesday.
Bogota's index gained 0.41 percent to 1,070.93 amid a 4.8 billion peso trade while Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.15 percent to 16,661.86 amid a 4.2 billion peso volume.

One Bogota broker said foreign funds were active, "trying to build up positions with relatively cheap shares in advance of" upcoming shareholders' assemblies. " One big gainer was Banco Ganadero, up 1.8 percent to 338 in Bogota and up 1.98 percent in Medellin to the same price.

Bancoquia bank also rose. It was up 1.51 percent in Bogota to 3,350 and up 2.42 percent to 3,380 in Medellin. Banco de Colombia, due to hold its shareholders assembly Friday, gained 0.47 percent in Bogota, closing at 426 pesos, and remained unchanged at 424.01 in Medellin.
"Shareholders are speculating that stock prices will rise when the Spanish banks move in," another Bogota broker said.
Spanish banks Banco Santander and Banco Central Hispano are due to buy stakes in Bancoquia and Banco de Colombia respectively in the near future.
Brewing giant Bavaria was also the target of foreign fund interest, rising 1.42 percent in Bogota to 6,900 and 1.47 percent to the same price in Medellin.
The biggest faller of the day was supermarket chain Cadenalco, down 2.27 percent to 861 in Medellin.
